note: Re-judged 2026-10-26 at HEAD dfabdcf8bf (independent judge, clean clone), after dd20e0aa1a changed removeZePolicy's unit. Section 4.4.1: "Every SPD SHOULD have a nominal, final entry that matches anything that is otherwise unmatched, and discards it." removeZePolicy's body is unchanged (RemovePolicyParams, then spdLeft.record); only its doc comment moved. The behaviour change is in spdLeftover.record, which now drops an entry from the ledger whenever policyGone accepts the removal answer: nil, ENOENT, PolicyOwnedError (left unrecorded as before), and isXFRMUnsupported (ErrNotSupported as before, now also the raw ENOPROTOOPT, EPROTONOSUPPORT, EAFNOSUPPORT and ENOSYS errnos). Those answers name a platform on which the entry never reached the dataplane, so the ledger still holds every entry a removal left, and releaseSPD still keeps the catch-all with a warning when any stays (warnSPDLeft). Residual note, not a defect: an XFRM kernel answering one of those errnos to a policy delete while the policy stays would let the catch-all go first; no such kernel answer is known for XFRM_MSG_DELPOLICY. applyConfig, installUnmatched, unmatchedPolicies, releaseSPD, shutdown, warnSPDLeft and parseUnmatched are unchanged. The three tagged units are unchanged and pass at HEAD under -race, the XFRM one executed, not skipped (TestRFC4301DefaultFinalSPDEntryDiscards, TestRFC4301FinalEntryIsUnderEveryZeSPDEntry, TestRFC4301InboundClearPacketIsDiscardedByTheDefaultFinalEntry), and TestReleaseSPDKeepsTheCatchAllWhenARemovalFails passes; their discrimination records (parseUnmatched reverts, the shutdown releaseSPD-first mutant) are current. Scope note carried from RFC4301-5.2-1: VPP holds no catch-all and the OSPFv3 RFC 4552 entries have none. spdLeftover.record and policyGone are added to the code map, because the ledger's answer now lives there. Verdict stands.
